correctness.rationale: Exact independent-row averaging reduces the dyadic random sign to a bounded periodic product. Fourier diagonalization of Binomial increments modulo a dyadic modulus yields uniform mixing faster than every positive power because 2^r <= n^gamma with gamma<1/2. Near/far temporal covariance splitting gives a polynomial L2 rate, a dense polynomial subsequence and interpolation give almost-sure Cesaro convergence, and bounded martingale differences yield the quenched functional CLT. Conditional fourth moments supply uniform integrability for the converse, and two-sided exponential bounds on the residue means give an exact density criterion. The standalone exact-rational checker passed 723 finite identities; it is not used as an infinite-time proof.

originality.rationale: The nearest 2026 paper proves annealed convergence in an inclusion-induced family with ellipticity for all coefficients. The active-only sparse dyadic model violates that ellipticity, and the earlier general bootstrap martingale theorem does not calculate this environment-specific quenched correlation nor its necessary-and-sufficient density criterion. value.rationale: The motivating random-bootstrap problem distinguishes annealed and quenched laws. A class using only O(log n) fresh random inclusion parameters per time obtains a complete quenched Brownian limit classification and a sharp natural-density independence condition. The Fourier mixing of time-varying dyadic residues yields an explicit structural mechanism; the conclusion is neither just finite arithmetic nor the unverified invocation of an abstract invariance principle.
